samples.task_summary: Predict whether an ACS person is employed, using person and household characteristics that generalize across states.

scores.rationale: Age is one of the strongest stable predictors of labor-force participation and employment.
Education strongly and consistently predicts employment opportunities across states.
Marital status has some stable association with employment but is mostly indirect and demographic.
Sex can correlate with employment patterns, but it is a sensitive demographic shortcut and less causally portable.
Disability status is a robust predictor of employment constraints and should generalize reasonably well.
Parent employment status is mainly meaningful for children and is weak or inapplicable for this adult employment task.
Recent mobility may weakly relate to employment transitions, but it is noisy and can reflect state-specific migration patterns.
Citizenship can affect labor market access, but it is a sensitive proxy with uneven state composition and policy effects.
Military service has some labor-market relevance but is a niche demographic marker with limited broad predictive value.
Ancestry is mostly a demographic proxy and likely captures brittle population composition rather than stable employment mechanisms.
Nativity can matter for employment, but it is a coarse sensitive proxy and may vary in composition across states.
Relationship to householder can reflect life stage and household structure, which have moderate stable links to employment.
Hearing difficulty is a meaningful functional limitation that can reduce employment likelihood across contexts.
Vision difficulty is a stable indicator of work-limiting disability and general employment barriers.
Cognitive difficulty is strongly relevant to employability and should transfer well across states.
Race can correlate with employment through structural factors, but it is a sensitive shortcut and less desirable for OOD robustness.
Grandparent-care status is highly specific and likely weakly related to employment for the general population.

Parent employment status is mainly defined for children and is not a meaningful predictor for this adult employment task.
Recent mobility can weakly relate to employment, but it is also geography-linked and potentially brittle.
Citizenship affects labor market access, but it can also act as a sensitive proxy with state-dependent effects.
Military service has limited direct relevance for employment and is a niche demographic marker.
Ancestry is a weak proxy likely to capture demographic and regional shortcuts rather than stable employment signal.
Nativity is moderately informative for labor market participation but can also encode sensitive immigrant-status effects.
Household relationship can reflect life stage and caregiving responsibilities, but it is only moderately predictive.
Hearing difficulty is a meaningful, stable indicator of work-limiting health constraints.
Vision difficulty is a stable health-related predictor of employment, though less central than education or age.
Cognitive difficulty is strongly and semantically tied to employment capacity across geographies.
Race is a sensitive attribute and mostly a proxy for structural and regional differences rather than direct task signal.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether an ACS respondent is employed, using person and household attributes that should generalize across states.

scores.rationale: Age is one of the strongest stable predictors of employment across states and reflects broad labor-force participation patterns.
Education is highly predictive of employment and tends to transfer well across geographies.
Marital status has some stable association with employment but is only a moderate proxy and not directly causal.
Sex can correlate with employment patterns, but it is a sensitive demographic shortcut and less desirable for robust generalization.
Disability status is strongly related to labor-force participation and is fairly stable, though it is sensitive and may encode structural barriers.
Parent employment status is mainly defined for children and is not a meaningful stable predictor for this adult employment task.
Recent mobility can weakly relate to employment transitions, but it is noisy and may capture state-specific migration patterns.
Citizenship status can affect employment access, but it is a sensitive proxy and may not generalize cleanly across states.
Military service status can be informative for labor-force attachment, but it is a niche and potentially cohort-specific signal.
Ancestry is usually a weak proxy for employment and risks encoding demographic or regional shortcuts.
Nativity can matter for employment outcomes, but it is a sensitive demographic attribute and only moderately useful.
Relationship to householder can capture household composition and life stage, which are moderately predictive in a stable way.
Hearing difficulty is a stable health-related predictor of employment, though less informative than age or education.
Vision difficulty has a real but moderate association with employment and is broadly portable across states.
Cognitive difficulty is a meaningful and stable predictor of employment limitations, though it is sensitive.
Race can correlate with employment through structural factors, but it is a sensitive shortcut and less desirable for OOD robustness.
Grandparent care status is relatively niche and likely weakly predictive, with limited stable signal for adult employment.
